title: The problem of copying links through the context menu and buttons

judgment.rationale: The current public evidence still points away from a clear PowerToys-owned fix path and toward a browser-side or clipboard-side behavior that is not localized to any enabled PowerToys feature.
evidence: The reporter says only Find My Mouse and Always On Top were enabled, neither of which owns browser share dialogs or URL copy formatting.
The only follow-up comment links an external browser-side report of similar malformed URL copy behavior.
The issue still does not identify a PowerToys module, hook, or reproducible PowerToys-only path that corrupts clipboard data on demand.
judgment.recommended_action: Do not queue a PowerToys design from the current evidence; wait for stronger module-localized proof before treating this as a PowerToys code bug.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current thread does not establish a concrete PowerToys-owned code path to change, so publishing a PowerToys fix plan would be more speculative than useful.

issue_context.summary: The reporter sees malformed strings copied from browser share/context-menu link actions, but the thread still does not connect that clipboard corruption to a specific PowerToys-owned feature path.
known_information: The issue was filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 and mentions Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge.
The reporter says the behavior disappears when PowerToys is exited and returns when it is restarted, but only Find My Mouse and Always On Top were enabled.
A bug report ZIP is attached, and the only comment so far links a public discussion of similar link-copy anomalies outside PowerToys.
inferences: The enabled-module list weakens the case for a PowerToys-owned clipboard transformation bug because neither named module is supposed to intercept browser share-copy output.
The current evidence may be describing a browser or OS clipboard quirk that merely correlates with PowerToys being present rather than being caused by an identifiable PowerToys module.
issue_context.analysis: This issue is currently better classified as not actionable than as a guessed fix plan. The report is real, but the thread still does not isolate a PowerToys component that owns the behavior, and there is already an external similarity signal in the discussion. A dashboard artifact should preserve that uncertainty instead of inventing a root cause.
initial_investigation: No linked PowerToys fix, maintainer repro, or product-area label has been added since the initial report.
The issue body itself says the only enabled PowerToys features were Find My Mouse and Always On Top, which do not directly explain browser-specific URL-copy corruption.
